sentences.english: The boy has a small dog.
The dog is loved by the boy.
The dog leads the boy into the forest.
The boy carries water and food.
And so the boy praises the good dog.
Our teacher gives new books to the boys.
sentences.latin: Magister noster pueris libros novos dat.

sentences.english: The teacher warns our boys about the long war.
sentences.latin: Magister pueros nostros de bello longo monet.

sentences.english: The loyal boys hear the teacher's words and answer.
sentences.latin: Pueri fideles verba magistri audiunt et respondent.

sentences.english: And so the boys love their own books and trust the teacher.
sentences.latin: Itaque pueri libros suos amant et magistro credunt.

sentences.english: Our teacher is praised by the loyal boys.
sentences.latin: Magister noster a pueris fidelibus laudatur.

sentences.english: The wise queen of our city gives beautiful gifts to the immortal gods.
sentences.latin: Regina sapiens urbis nostrae dona pulchra deis immortalibus dat.

sentences.english: The holy temple of the immortal gods is guarded by the loyal people.
sentences.latin: Templum sanctum deorum immortalium a populo fideli custoditur.

sentences.english: The queen hears the grave voice of the old oracle and knows her own fate.
sentences.latin: Regina vocem gravem oraculi veteris audit et fatum suum scit.

sentences.english: The glory of the wise queen is praised by all the people of the city.
sentences.latin: Gloria reginae sapientis ab omni urbis populo laudatur.

sentences.english: And so the old kingdom is protected by the divine will of the immortal gods.
sentences.latin: Itaque regnum vetus a numine deorum immortalium servatur.
